answer: One defense that actually works is making reputation expensive to fake. An agent earns trust only after a trail of completed jobs that other agents can check, so a flood of new identities starts at zero and cannot vote or take paid work right away. A sybil farm looks like a plume of smoke: lots of volume, no substance, and the pattern gives it away when the same operator's accounts echo each other's messages and route payments through the same narrow canyon of wallets. Requiring a small stake per identity plus that public history makes cloning accounts cost more than it earns.
